units.description: Whether the whole of s is a dot-separated list of identifiers: at least one identifier, every identifier non-empty and made only of ASCII letters, digits and '-' (so no empty text, no leading, trailing or doubled dot, no '_' or space). If no_zero is true, an identifier made only of digits must not have a leading zero ("0" is fine, "01" is not, "0a" is fine since it has a letter); if no_zero is false leading zeros are allowed. This is the check for a PRERELEASE (no_zero true) and for BUILD metadata (no_zero false), applied to the text after the '-' or '+', not including it. It must never panic on any bytes.
tests: fn list_is(s: &static [byte], nz: bool, want: bool) -> [] int { if ident_list_ok(s, nz) == want { return 0; } return 1; }

units.description: Whether s is a valid version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]. Exactly three numbers separated by dots; each is 1 to 9 ASCII digits with no leading zero (the single digit "0" is fine). Then optionally '-' and a PRERELEASE, then optionally '+' and BUILD; the PRERELEASE is the text from the first '-' after the patch number up to the first '+' (or the end), and a '-' inside it is just an identifier character ("1.2.3-a-b" is valid). A '-' or '+' with nothing after it is invalid. The prerelease and the build are checked with ident_list_ok (no leading zero in an all-digit PRERELEASE identifier, leading zeros allowed in BUILD). No leading 'v', no whitespace anywhere, no fourth number. Never panics on any bytes.

units.description: Precedence of two PRERELEASE lists, each already valid and given without the leading '-' (for example "alpha.1" or "rc.2"): -1 if a is lower than b, 0 if equal, 1 if a is higher. Compare identifier by identifier from the left. Two all-digit identifiers compare as numbers ("2" < "11"; there are no leading zeros, and an identifier can be 9 digits or more, so compare without overflowing, for example by length first); any other pair compares as ASCII text byte by byte (upper case sorts before lower case); an all-digit identifier is lower than one that is not. When every shared identifier is equal, the list with fewer identifiers is lower. The result is exactly -1, 0 or 1, never another number.
tests: fn pre_is(a: &static [byte], b: &static [byte], want: int) -> [] int { if pre_compare(a, b) == want { return 0; } return 1; }

units.description: Err(message) if either text is not a valid version (use semver_valid), otherwise Ok(-1), Ok(0) or Ok(1) by semantic-versioning precedence: a lower than b, equal, higher. MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH compare numerically, in that order ("1.2.3" < "1.10.0"). A version with a PRERELEASE is lower than the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without one; two PRERELEASE lists compare with pre_compare. BUILD metadata (after '+') is ignored entirely. The Ok value is exactly -1, 0 or 1, never another number. Never panics on any bytes.
tests: fn cmp_is(a: &static [byte], b: &static [byte], want: int) -> [] int { match semver_compare(a, b) { result.Result::Ok(v) => { if v == want { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
fn cmp_err(a: &static [byte], b: &static [byte]) -> [] int { match semver_compare(a, b) { result.Result::Ok(_) => { return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }

units.description: Whether version satisfies ONE comparator (no spaces in it): an optional operator directly followed by a full version. Err(message) if version is not a valid version, or the comparator is not an operator ('=', '>', '>=', '<', '<=', '^', '~' or none, where none means '=') directly followed by a valid version (so "!=1.2.3", "^1.2", "^", "" and "> 1.2.3" are Err; read '>=' and '<=' as one operator, not as '>' then '='). Otherwise Ok(bool), all by precedence (the same ordering as semver_compare, BUILD ignored): '=' equal, '>' '>=' '<' '<=' as written. '~X.Y.Z' means >=X.Y.Z and <X.(Y+1).0. '^X.Y.Z' means >=X.Y.Z and below the next change of the left-most non-zero number: <(X+1).0.0 if X>0, else <0.(Y+1).0 if Y>0, else <0.0.(Z+1). The comparator's version may carry a PRERELEASE and then takes part in the lower bound by normal precedence; the upper bound has no prerelease, so "2.0.0-rc.1" is below "2.0.0" and satisfies "^1.5.0". There is no special rule for prerelease versions.
tests: fn hold_is(v: &static [byte], c: &static [byte], want: bool) -> [] int { match comparator_holds(v, c) { result.Result::Ok(x) => { if x == want { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
fn hold_err(v: &static [byte], c: &static [byte]) -> [] int { match comparator_holds(v, c) { result.Result::Ok(_) => { return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }

units.description: Err(message) if the version is invalid or the range is invalid, otherwise Ok(whether the version satisfies the range). A range is one or more comparators separated by EXACTLY ONE space; the version must satisfy all of them (use comparator_holds for each). Invalid ranges, all Err: the empty range, a leading, trailing or doubled space (so an empty piece between spaces), an unknown operator, a space between operator and version (">= 1.0.0"), a partial version ("^1.2"), any piece that is not a valid comparator. The whole range is checked: a bad comparator later in the range is an Err even if an earlier one already failed, and the version is checked as well (invalid version with a fine range is Err). Never panics on any bytes.
tests: fn sat_is(v: &static [byte], r: &static [byte], want: bool) -> [] int { match semver_satisfies(v, r) { result.Result::Ok(x) => { if x == want { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
fn sat_err(v: &static [byte], r: &static [byte]) -> [] int { match semver_satisfies(v, r) { result.Result::Ok(_) => { return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
